title: Same breakout rules on NQ, ES and gold over ten years: +91.8%, +30.3% and -48.2%
author: person-person12
selftext:
Something i see constantly is somebody finding rules that hold up on NQ and then putting the exact same thing on ES or gold because its the same idea on a different market. I had one set of rules in front of me so i ran it on three and left everything else alone.

20 candle high breakout, 15 minute candles, long only, 1 ATR stop, 2 ATR target, full session. 29 May 2016 to 1 October 2026, 100k account, one contract. Same code on all three, only the symbol changed, and commission and slippage charged on entry and exit. Between 242,000 and 245,000 candles each in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading).

**NQ:** 3,201 trades, 40.9% wins, profit factor 1.09, **+91.8%**, max drawdown 16.3%

**ES:** 3,093 trades, 38.8% wins, profit factor 1.05, **+30.3%**, max drawdown 16.0%

**GC (gold):** 1,911 trades, 37.4% wins, profit factor 0.90, **-48.2%**, max drawdown 53.2%

The three win rates sit inside 3.5 points of each other, so **the thing separating +91.8% from -48.2% was never how often the rules were right.** On NQ the average winner is big enough to carry a 40% hit rate and on gold it isnt, and thats the gap.

The drawdown is the part id actually care about if i were going to trade one of them. NQ and ES both held around 16% while gold ran to 53.2%, so on a 100k account thats 16k of open loss against 53k, on rules that read identically on paper.

**\_\_\_\_\_**

Gold moves differently to an index and a plain breakout is not a sensible read on it, so gold coming last of the three is not a shock. What i did not expect was the size of it. Theres no version of these rules that was tuned to NQ, its a 20 candle high with an ATR stop and an ATR target, about as unfitted as a breakout gets, and NQ still came out at three times ES over the same decade on identical code.

So the market was doing more of the work here than the rules were, and i could not have told you that from the NQ run on its own.

The only line i changed between the three runs was the symbol.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: A clean test, and since the three win rates are so close, the real gap is average winner versus average loser, so I'd show those numbers per market. NQ and ES share a strong trending decade, so a cross-market check that adds a market with a different history, such as a sideways or falling stretch, would show whether the rules or the market drove the results. Also check the trade counts: 3,000 trades on 15-minute candles cluster into a few trending periods, so the number of independent episodes is much smaller. Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for macro releases) is one source for tagging the news days that make up the big runners.

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body:
Agreed on avg winner vs avg loser, thats the number that actually separates the three and it should have been sitting next to the win rates instead of me leaving you to ask for it.

The independent episodes point is the one i think is most right. **3,000 trades on 15m candles is nowhere near 3,000 independent samples**, theyre bunched into a handful of trending stretches, so the real sample is much smaller than the trade count makes it look. Gold was supposed to be the different-history leg and it came out -48.2%, but gold has had a run of its own so it isnt really the sideways case you mean.

What would you use for the falling stretch, 2022 on its own or something longer?

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Something longer, if you can get it. 2022 alone is a single episode, so it tells you how the rules behave in that one regime and little else. A stretch that includes 2022 plus a few other sideways or falling periods (for example 2018 and mid-2015 to early 2016, if your data goes back) gives you several separate episodes. Even then, report it as episodes, not trades, and name the dates before you run it. Thanks for taking the points on board, and I'll look out for the results.

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body: Naming them before I run it, as asked: Jan to Dec 2018, Jan 2022 to Dec 2022, and Aug 2015 to Mar 2016. My history on NQ starts mid 2016 so that last one only exists on ES and gold, and Ill say which markets each episode covers rather than averaging across them. Reported per episode, not pooled into one trade count.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: That's the right setup: dates fixed first, per episode, and clear about which markets each one covers. Thanks for running it, and I'll look out for the results.
